decision_conditions: Secured by DesignThe development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Certificate of Compliance in accordance with Secured by Design - Residential Guide 2025 (or the relevant Secured by Design Guide(s) or an achieved Crime Prevention Standard) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, secure, sustainable communities

Digital InfrastructureThe development hereby approved shall be fitted with superfast broadband capability prior to first occupation and be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interest of ensuring the provision of appropriate digital infrastructure in accordance with Policy SI6 of the London Plan (2021)

Restricted UseNotwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) and the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015, or any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting those Orders, the development hereby approved shall be used only for purposes falling within Use Class B2 (General Industrial), Use Class B8 (Storage or Distribution) and Use Class E(g)(iii) (Industrial Processes), and for no other purpose.Reason: To ensure that the use of the premises remains appropriate to the character of the area and the assessment of the application, and to prevent the introduction of alternative uses that could give rise to unacceptable impacts on amenity, traffic or the local environment without further consideration by the Local Planning Authority

Transport ModellingAs part of the Reserved Matters application for access, an updated Transport Assessment and associated modelling shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The updated assessment shall take account of prevailing traffic conditions, development phasing, committed development and any changes in policy or network operation at the time of submission. Where required, the assessment shall include revised trip generation, distribution and assignment, junction capacity assessments and any mitigation measures necessary to demonstrate the continued acceptability of the development in transport and highway terms.The development shall thereafter be carried out in full accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the development continues to provide safe and suitable access and does not result in an unacceptable impact on the transport network, having regard to changes in background traffic levels, delivery phasing and relevant policy requirements

EV Charging PointsEach application for the approval of Reserved Matters shall be accompanied by details of Electric Vehicular Charging Points (EVCPs) serving the development hereby approved. The details shall include the number, siting and specification of the EVCPs and demonstrate how they will be provided in accordance with the relevant standards of the approved Design Code dated December 2025 and the London Plan unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All active electric vehicle charging facilities shall be installed and made available for use prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To ensure that the development provides adequate electric vehicle charging infrastructure in accordance with Local Plan and London Plan policy requirements

Vehicle Parking and Turning and Disable Parking FacilitiesNo development shall commence until details of parking, turning and disabled persons parking facilities have been submitted as part of the Reserved Matters application for access and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with the standards adopted by the Local Planning Authority and the London Plan, including a minimum of 5 per cent of the total parking provision as designated disabled persons parking bays and a minimum of 5 per cent as enlarged bays capable of conversion to designated disabled persons parking bays, in accordance with Policy T6.5 of the London Plan (2021). The details shall also be in line with the approved provision set out in the outline application.The approved parking, turning and disabled parking facilities shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the relevant phase of the development and shall thereafter be retained for their intended purpose.Reason: To ensure that the development complies with Local Plan and London Plan policies and to ensure that adequate parking and turning and disabled parking facilities are provided in the interests of highway safety and the free flow of traffic on adjoining highways

Submission of Reserved MattersNo part of the development hereby permitted shall be begun until details of the following reserved matters have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:(a) access(b) appearance(c) landscaping(d) layout(e) scaleAll applications for approval of all Reserved Matters shall be made to the Local Planning Authority no later than five years from the date of this permission.The commencement of the development pursuant to this outline consent shall begin before the expiration of two years from the date of the final approval of the last reserved matter to be approved.The development shall be carried out as approved.Reason: To prevent the accumulation of unimplemented planning permissions and in accordance with the requirements of section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004

Parameter PlansThe detailed design of the development proposed through each Reserved Matters application pursuant to this outline planning permission shall accord with the parameters defined in the approved Parameters Plans listed below. No Reserved Matters application shall be approved which proposes development outside of those parameters unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority:23126-UMC-ZZZZ-SI-DR-A-0504.P15 Parameters Plan - Site Wide; and 23126-UMC-ZZZZ-SI-DR-A-0511.P06 Parameters Plan - Zone A HeightsReason: To ensure that the detailed proposals brought forward at Reserved Matters stage remain within the scope of the development assessed as part of the outline application and to retain appropriate control over the design of the development

Construction Logistics Management PlanPrior to the commencement of any construction activities on the site, a comprehensive Construction Logistics Management Plan (CLMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Planning Authority for approval. The CLMP shall address the following key aspects:1.          Site Access and Egress:o Detail the proposed routes for construction vehicles to access and exit the site.o Provide measures to minimise traffic congestion and disruptions to the surrounding road network.o Specify any proposed temporary road closures or diversions, if applicable.2.          Construction Traffic Management:o Outline arrangements for the management of construction traffic, including loading and unloading areas.o Confirmation of designated times for deliveries to minimise impact on peak traffic hours.o Provide measures to ensure the safe passage of pedestrians and cyclists around the site.3.          Site Layout and Storage:o Provide a site layout plan indicating the location of construction activities, storage areas, and welfare facilities.o Detail provisions for the storage of materials, equipment, and waste to minimise visual and environmental impact.o Specify measures to mitigate noise, dust, and other nuisances generated by construction activities.4.          Construction Schedule:o Present a construction schedule outlining the sequence of works and anticipated duration of each phase, including number and type of vehicles required for each stage.o Detail the hours of work expected for each phase and the overall duration.5.          Health and Safety:o Demonstrate compliance with health and safety regulations, including provisions for worker safety and welfare.o Detail measures to mitigate risks associated with construction activities, such as traffic accidents and site hazards.o Arrangements for wheel cleaning.o Measures to use operators committed to best practice, demonstrated by membership of TfL's Freight Operator Recognition Scheme (FORS), or similar6. Photographic condition survey:o Provide photographic condition survey of the public adopted highway leading up to the site including the footways, before any work commences.Development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved CLMP.Reason: To ensure that the impact of the development on the surrounding transport network is sufficiently assessed and where necessary appropriately mitigated in accordance with policy DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021)

Cycle Parking & End-of-Trip Facilities ConditionEach application for the approval of Reserved Matters shall be accompanied by details of cycle parking and associated end-of-trip facilities serving the development hereby approved. The details shall demonstrate compliance with the approved Design Code dated December 2025, London Plan Policy T5 and the London Cycling Design Standards and shall include:o The required number of long-stay and short-stay cycle spaces;o Secure, covered, and easily accessible long-stay provision;o Provision for non-standard cycles; ando End-of-trip facilities for users, including showers, lockers and changing facilities (where applicable to the use).The approved facilities shall be fully provided prior to first occupation and retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure adequate and inclusive cycle parking and supporting facilities in accordance with London Plan Policy T5 and to promote active travel

Waste ManagementNo above ground works shall commence until details of refuse and recycling storage facilities to be provided within the development and a detailed Operational Waste Management Plan have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The approved refuse and recycling facilities and management plan shall be provided and implemented in full accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interests of amenity and to ensure the appropriate storage and recycling of waste materials in support of the Borough's waste reduction and recycling objectives

Delivery and Servicing PlanNo above ground works shall commence until a Delivery and Servicing Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan should include:a. details of vehicle types, expected frequencies and loading and unloading locationsb. an assessment of delivery and servicing activity in relation to peak periods on the surrounding highway networkc. links to the Travel Plan and Parking Management Plan secured through the Section 106 Agreement where applicabled. details of proposed access routesThe approved Delivery and Servicing Plan shall be implemented prior to the occupation of the development and shall thereafter be complied with for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that delivery and servicing activities are managed effectively so as to minimise impacts on the highway network, safeguard the amenities of nearby residential occupiers and promote highway safety

External Materials(a) No above ground works shall take place until detailed drawings and a schedule of materials and products of all external facing materials to be used in the construction of the building hereby approved, along with material sample boards, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Detailed drawings shall include:- Principal features on the facades e.g. window study (1:50 @ A1) - Details of each envelope / roof type (1:20 @A3)- Details of glazing and curtain walling systems (1:20 @A3) - Key junctions/bonds between materials/finishes (1:20 @A3) - Building entrances, glazing and signage zones, vented panels to plant rooms, workspace frontages (1:50 @ A1) - Parapets, roof edges, rooftop plant screening, lift over runs (1:20 @A3) - Elevational location of all joints - structural, movement, panels (1:100 @ A1) - Elevational location of all items which are fixed to the façade e.g. rainwater pipes, lighting, CCTV, alarms (1:100 @ A1)Samples of materials and products shall include: - Façade and roof cladding materials - Window / door types (including all finishes, glass types and any manifestation) - Curtain wall (including finishes, glass types and any manifestation) - Facing metalwork (e.g. service doors, screens, gates) - All items which are fixed / integrated to the façade (e.g. fins/louvres, vent grilles, rainwater pipes, signage)(b) The sample boards required in (a) shall be made available on site for inspection by the Local Planning Authority and the approved sample boards shall be retained on site for the duration of the construction works.(c) The development shall not be occupied until it has been carried out in full accordance with the approved details and shall thereafter be retained as approved.Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development is acceptable and contributes towards a high quality built environment

Design CodeEach application for the approval of Reserved Matters shall be in accordance with the hereby approved Design Code (UMC Architects dated December 2025) unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority through the Reserved Matters applications.Reason: To ensure full compliance with the outline application hereby approved and to prevent harm arising through deviations from the approved plans in accordance with the relevant policy framework

Development ThresholdsThe development hereby approved shall comply with the following development thresholds:(a) a minimum gross internal floorspace of 33,014 square metres and a maximum gross internal floorspace of 68,000 square metres; and(b) a maximum building height of 36 metres above finished floor level.No Reserved Matters application shall be approved which would result in development exceeding these thresholds unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the approval plans and other submitted details and to ensure that the detailed proposals brought forward at Reserved Matters stage remain within the scope of the development assessed as part of the outline application

Hard Surfacing MaterialsNo above ground works shall take place until full details of hard landscape works of all open areas and public realm have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Hard landscape details shall include:a) details of any proposed earthworks and proposed finished levels or contours including any alterations in existing ground levels and excavationsb) details of vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areasc) details of inclusive design including external steps and ramps, tactile warning or wayfinding paving, mobility features and dropped kerbsd) hard surfacing materials which shall be permeable as appropriate, including dimensions, bonding and pointinge) minor artefacts and structures e.g. street furniture, refuse or other storage units, signage, lighting, ecological enhancements, bollards and any hostile vehicle mitigationf) boundary treatmentg) location of services above and below ground including service trenches, drainage, power, access covers and supports to ensure no conflicts with tree and planting pits and integration of access covers with paving/surfacing layouth) materials samplesThe development shall not be occupied until it has been carried out in accordance with the approved details. The development shall thereafter be retained as such.Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development is acceptable and contributes towards a high quality built environment

External Building Services Plant Visual & Acoustic ScreeningNo above ground works shall take place until detailed drawings (1:5 and 1:20, materials, products and acoustic attenuation performance for external building services plant visual & acoustic screening has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Authority. This should include identification of impacted nearby sensitive receptors and screening design and performance to suit. The development shall not be occupied until it has been carried out in accordance with the approved details. The development shall thereafter be retained as such.Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development is acceptable and contributes towards a high quality built environment

Wayfinding and Signage StrategyNo above ground works shall take place until details of a Wayfinding and Signage Strategy, including wayfinding, waymarking from points of arrival, street signage and traffic related signage has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include the proposed locations, design details, fittings and supporting structures for all signage. The development shall not be occupied until the approved Strategy has been implemented in full accordance with the approved details and it shall thereafter be retained as approved.Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development is acceptable and contributes towards a high quality built environment and to ensure that signage is designed and located in a manner that promotes the safe movement of pedestrians and vehicles

Public Realm Management and Maintenance StrategyPrior to the occupation of any part of the development a Public Realm Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall set out the long term management and maintenance arrangements for all areas of public realm within the site and shall include details of management responsibilities, maintenance regimes, cleansing arrangements, lighting, landscaping, refuse and litter management, safety and security measures, and public access arrangements.The approved Public Realm Management Plan shall be implemented in full prior to first occupation of the development and shall thereafter be adhered to for the lifetime of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the public realm is properly managed and maintained in the interests of visual amenity safety and the quality and usability of the public environment and to secure the long-term success of the development

Completion of Public RealmNo part of the development shall be occupied until the public realm works along Lincoln Road, identified in yellow as "Public Realm including hard and soft landscaping" on the approved Parameters Plan (Drawing No. 23126-UMC-ZZZZ-SI-DR-A-0504 Rev P15 - Parameters Plan: Site Wide) and as approved at the Reserved Matters stage, have been practically completed and made available for use. The approved public realm works shall thereafter be retained and maintained as approved.Reason: To ensure the timely delivery of the public realm along Lincoln Road as an integral component of the overall development and to secure a coordinated and coherent approach to the implementation of the scheme

External Lighting Strategy and Light SpillPrior to the commencement of the development, a comprehensive external lighting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include all external lighting, including security lighting and the illumination of buildings at night, and shall cover any lighting or light sources that may result in external light spill.The scheme shall include:i. the function of the proposed lighting and the uses it supportsii. a lux plan showing proposed and existing retained light sourcesiii. details of lighting height, design, orientation, beam angle and surface finish and colouriv. details of colour temperature of lighting and associated public realm surfaces including reflectivity and glarev. details of time limits on lighting and hours of operationvi. details of fixtures and any supporting structuresvii. details of measures to mitigate any potential impacts on residential amenity and biodiversity arising from the installation or operation of the lightingThe development shall not be occupied until the approved lighting scheme has been implemented in full accordance with the approved details. The lighting shall thereafter be retained and maintained as approved for the lifetime of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that external lighting provides a high quality and safe environment, protects the amenity of neighbouring occupiers and future occupants, avoids unnecessary light spill and glare and safeguards biodiversity interests that may be affected by artificial lighting

Impact PilingNo impact piling shall take place unless details of the proposed piling method have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Impact piling shall thereafter only be carried out in full accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect the amenity of nearby occupiers from noise and disturbance arising from construction activities

Acoustic ReportNo occupation of the development shall take place until an acoustic report, prepared in accordance with the methodology set out in BS4142:2014+A1:2019, and details of acoustic screening and other noise control measures have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall assess the noise generated by the proposed mechanical plant and identify the noise control measures necessary to ensure that the rating level from the plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical background noise level (measured as LA90,15min) during operational hours, when assessed at the façade of the nearest or most noise-sensitive residential property. The approved noise control measures shall be implemented in full prior to occupation and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To safeguard the amenities of nearby occupiers by preventing noise and disturbance

Non-Road Mobile Machinery(a) Prior to the commencement of development, evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The registration shall enable ongoing details of all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant with a net power rating between 37kW and 560kW to be uploaded for the duration of the demolition and construction phases of the development.(b) Prior to the commencement of demolition and construction works, evidence shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that all plant and machinery to be used on site will meet Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/EC (or any subsequent replacement standard) for both NOx and particulate matter emissions.(c) Throughout the demolition site preparation and construction phases of the development, an up-to-date inventory and emissions record for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery shall be maintained on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and shall include evidence of compliance with the relevant emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by officers of the Local Planning Authority upon request until completion of the development.Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health

ContaminationPrior to the occupation of the development the following documents shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:1) A Site Investigation scheme to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those off site. The results of the site investigation to be summarised via a generic or detailed quantitative risk assessment with conclusions and recommendations for clear actions, where required.Reason: To ensure that contaminated land is properly treated and made safe safeguard the health and safety of the future occupants in accordance with Policies CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD66 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)2) If required, a Remedial Options Appraisal and/or Remediation Strategy giving full details of the remediation and mitigation measures required and how they are to be undertaken.3) Where remediation is required,i) a Verification Plan setting out the details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy are complete to a satisfactory standard;ii) A Monitoring and Maintenance Plan, setting out provisions for long-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action; andiii) the development in the relevant Phase shall not be occupied until a post completion remediation Verification Report for that Phase, including results of sampling and monitoring carried out, has first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the site remediation criteria have been met.Reason: To ensure that contaminated land is properly treated and made safe safeguard the health and safety of the future occupants in accordance with Policies CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD66 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)4) If, during any phase of development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present within that phase, no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority) shall take place in that phase until an addendum remediation strategy, detailing how the previously unidentified contamination will be addressed, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved addendum remediation strategy shall be fully implemented prior to the occupation of any part of the development within that phase.Reason: To safeguard groundwater quality and human health in accordance with Policies CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD66 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)

Air QualityThe development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Air Quality Assessment ref. 33433-HYD-ZZ-XX-YY-RP-2001 Rev P03, prepared by Stantec, dated 16 May 2025. In addition, the mitigation measures set out in Section 8 of the assessment shall be implemented in full at the relevant part of the development.Reason: To ensure that the development does not result in an unacceptable impact on local air quality and to secure appropriate mitigation where necessary, in accordance with Policy SI 1 of the London Plan and the London Plan Sustainable Design and Construction Supplementary Planning Guidance

Biodiversity Net GainPrior to the commencement of the development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990. The Biodiversity Gain Plan shall use reasonable endeavours to achieve a minimum biodiversity net gain of 220% above the pre-development baseline as illustrated in Ecological Appraisal Report Rev A prepared by FPCR Environment and Design dated 29.05.2025. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan.Reason: To ensure the delivery and long-term maintenance of biodiversity net gain, to secure the biodiversity benefit of the scheme as identified in the approved proposals, and to comply with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by Schedule 14 of the Environment Act 2021), LP Policy G6 and DMD Policies 78 and 79.

Wind and MicroclimateEach application for the approval of Reserved Matters shall be accompanied by an updated Wind Desk-Based Assessment prepared by a suitably qualified consultant. The assessment shall have regard to Pedestrian Level Wind Desk-Based Assessment RWDI #2600443 Rev B prepared by RWDI dated 22.09.2025; be based on the detailed building design at that stage; and shall include appropriate plans and written commentary demonstrating that mitigation measures integrated into the design of buildings and/or interventions within the public realm, ensuring that, unless otherwise agreed with the Local Planning Authority,:(i) in the windiest season, the development achieves as a minimum a site-wide pedestrian comfort standard of "standing" across pedestrian thoroughfares and building entrances; and(ii) in the summer season, the development achieves as a minimum a pedestrian comfort standard of "sitting" for any bench amenity spaces in the public realm area identified in the Parameters Plan - Site Wide 23126-UMC-ZZZZ-SI-DR-A-0504 Rev P15 and a minimum pedestrian comfort standard of "standing" for all other areas.The development shall thereafter be carried out in full accordance with the approved mitigation measures.Reason: To ensure an acceptable level of pedestrian and occupier comfort within the development and the surrounding public realm

Tree ProtectionPrior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plans (TPP) for each stage of the development i.e. demolition, construction and landscaping. The plans shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a) location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);b) methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c) details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;d) a full specification for the construction of all roads, paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of internal roads and hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;e) detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;f) a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;g) a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;h) a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);i) details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;j) methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping following the works, if required.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) of the Development Management Document (2014) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

Tree PlantingNotwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved, whichever is the sooner, full details of all proposed tree planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include:a) a written specification for the planting, establishment and maintenance of new trees, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of locations;b) species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times;c) tree pit design (where appropriate), support systems, and;d) underground modular systems (where appropriate).e) How the proposed tree planting is compatible with the drainage strategy and other utilities.Any trees that are found to be dead, dying, severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced in the next planting season by specimens of similar size and species in the first suitable planting season.Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with the Biodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document (2014) and the London Plan (2021)

Soft LandscapingNo above ground works shall take place until above ground details of the hard and soft landscape treatment of all parts on the site not covered by buildings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The site shall be landscaped strictly in accordance with the approved details in the first planting season after completion or first occupation of the development, whichever is the sooner. Details shall include:1)            a scaled plan showing all existing vegetation and landscape features to be retained and all trees and plants to be planted;2)            location, type and materials to be used for hard landscaping including specifications, where applicable for:a) permeable pavingb) sustainable urban drainage integrationc) use within tree Root Protection Areas (RPAs);d) a schedule detailing sizes and numbers/densities of all proposed trees/plants;e) specifications for operations associated with plant establishment and maintenance that are compliant with best practise; and3)            types, materials, design and dimensions of all boundary treatments.4)           How the proposed landscaping is compatible with the drainage strategy and other utilities.There shall be no excavation or raising or lowering of levels within the prescribed root protection area of retained trees other than has already been agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Unless required by a separate landscape management condition, all soft landscaping shall have a written five-year maintenance programme following planting. Any new planting (other than trees) that is removed or becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced with new planting. Unless further specific permission has been given by the Local Planning Authority, replacement planting shall be in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with the Biodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document (2014) and the London Plan (2021)

Ecology(a) The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved Ecological Appraisal Report Rev A prepared by FPCR Environment and Design Ltd dated May 2025 and shall be carried out in accordance with the mitigation and enhancement measures and set out in Section 6.0.(b) Prior to the commencement of above ground works, details of the siting and number of bat boxes/bricks/tiles and bird bricks/tubes/boxes designed into and around the new buildings and trees, under the supervision of a suitably qualified ecologist, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.(c) Prior to the first occupation of the development, details confirming the installation of the approved bat boxes/bricks/tiles and bird bricks/tubes/boxes, together with photographic evidence, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved ecological features shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the development is undertaken in accordance with the Ecological Appraisal Report submitted and all measures identified therein to mitigate the impact of the development on the environment are fully complied with and enhance the ecological value

SuDSThe development shall not commence until a Sustainable Drainage Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The details shall be based on the disposal of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system in accordance with the principles as set out in the Technical Guidance to the National Planning Policy Framework and should be in line with our DMD Policy SuDS Requirements:a) Shall be designed to a 1 in 1 and 1 in 100 year storm event with the allowance for climate changeb) Follow the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy and providing evidence of the potential for full infiltration SuDS and maximising above ground storagec) Follow the SuDS management train by providing source control for the site, and a number of treatment phases corresponding to their pollution potential d) Maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation valuee) The system must be designed to allow for flows that exceed the design capacity to be stored on site or conveyed off-site with minimum impactf) Clear ownership, management and maintenance arrangements must be establishedg) The details submitted shall include levels, sizing, cross sections and specifications for all drainage featuresh) Pay the Offsite Drainage Contribution pursuant to the Section 106 Agreement if 100% discharge cannot be achieved via source control SuDS measuresReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy (2010), DMD Policy 61 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value

SuDS VerificationPrior to occupation of the development, a Verification Report demonstrating that the approved SuDS and Flood Risk measures have been fully implemented shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This report must include:o As built drawings of the sustainable drainage systems including level information (if appropriate)o Photographs of the completed sustainable drainage systemso Any relevant certificates from manufacturers/ suppliers of any drainage featureso A confirmation statement of the above signed by the site manager or similarReason : Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy (2010), DMD Policy 61 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value

District Energy NetworkWith each Reserved Matters application, details demonstrating that a safeguarded route for future district heating pipework from the public highway through the site will be provided and kept free of obstructions and conflicting services to enable a future connection to a District Heat Network shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets by renewable energy are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010)  and Policy SI 2 of the London Plan (2021)

Energy Statement(a) With each Reserved Matters application, notwithstanding the Energy Statement submitted, an Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Energy Statement shall demonstrate how the development accords with the Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the energy hierarchy to minimise carbon emissions arising from the operation of the development and its services, as committed to at the design stage, and shall include details of all proposed mitigation measures and energy efficiency measures to reduce energy demand and carbon emissions. The Energy Statement shall also include details of the Carbon Offset Compensation required to offset any remaining regulated carbon emissions.(b) Following the practical completion of the development, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The updated Energy Statement shall confirm the measures implemented in practice and the final New Development Carbon Compensation required for that phase. The confirmed carbon offset contribution shall be paid in full prior to the occupation of any building unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.(c) The development shall be implemented in full accordance with the approved Energy Statement and the mitigation measures and energy saving measures set out within it prior to the occupation of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and Policy SI 2 of the London Plan (2021)

Overheating RiskWith each submission of Reserved Matters, an Overheating Assessment, prepared in accordance with the principles contained in the Outline Energy and Sustainability Strategy Rev P4 dated 28 May 2025, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Overheating Assessment and any approved overheating strategy. All passive and active mitigation measures identified to prevent overheating shall be fully installed and operational prior to the first occupation of the development. The approved mitigation measures shall thereafter be retained and maintained in an operational condition for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that suitable living conditions are achieved within the development and that the buildings do not overheat, in accordance with policy SI4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014)

BREEAMThe development hereby approved shall achieve a BREEAM rating of 'Excellent' or higher or an equivalent independent measure of energy performance and sustainability. Where the performance of the development is measured using BREEAM, it shall achieve not less than the total credits for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories in the BREEAM Pre- Assessment hereby approved.A post completion certificate (or equivalent certification) confirming that the development has been completed in accordance with the required BREEAM rating and has maintained or exceeded the approved total credit scores for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority within six months of first occupation of the development.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and Policy SI 2 of the London Plan (2021)

Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment(a) Each application for reserved matters shall be accompanied by a detailed Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Statement in line with the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Assessment Guidance, which shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The statement shall adhere to the principles set out in the Whole Life Carbon Report Rev PO1 dated 20 August 2025. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so approved.(b) Prior to the occupation of the development, the post-construction tab of the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment template should be completed in line with the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment Guidance. The template together with any supporting information shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the development minimises carbon emissions throughout its whole life cycle in accordance with Policy SI2 OF the London Plan (2021) and Mayor of London's guidance 'Whole Life-cycle Carbon Assessments' (March 2022)

Circular Economy Statement(a) With each Reserved Matters Application, a Circular Economy Statement in line with the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.(b) Prior to occupation, a report in line with the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority evidencing how the Circular Economy Goals and Commitments in the pre-construction Circular Economy Statement have been satisfied.Reason: To ensure the development is resource efficient and maintains products and materials at their highest use for as long as possible in accordance with Policy SI7 of the London Plan (202) and Mayor of London's guidance Circular Economy (March 2022)

Fire SafetyPrior to the commencement of any construction activities on the site, a Fire Statement in accordance with Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details thus approved.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures

Water Network InfrastructureNo part of the development shall be occupied until written confirmation has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority that either:- all necessary water network upgrades required to accommodate the additional demand arising from the development have been completed; or- a development and infrastructure phasing plan has been agreed with Thames Water.Where a development and infrastructure phasing plan has been agreed, no occupation shall take place other than in full accordance with the approved development and infrastructure phasing plan.Reason: To ensure that sufficient water supply infrastructure capacity is available to accommodate the additional demand generated by the development and to ensure the proper and coordinated provision of essential infrastructure
